summary: Elevated tail latency for tool-enabled completions due to synchronous tool-proxy handshake and per-invocation schema compilation
description: Issue summary: Customer AcmePayments reports large increases in P95/P99 end-to-end latency for completions that include tool/function calls. The regression appears to correlate with a recent change in the function-proxy handshake and an aggressive per-invocation JSON schema compilation step in the validator. Impact: Several customer endpoints experiencing 2x-4x tail latency increases during peak hours, causing timeouts in the customer's checkout flow. Business impact: failed authorizations and elevated error rates for enterprise production traffic. Environment: prod, us-east-1, dedicated enterprise tenant for AcmePayments. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a completion request with 3 sequential tool calls (validate_card -> check_balance -> create_auth) using the customer's tool adapter config. 2) Observe traces via /trace endpoint and measure end-to-end latency for tool-enabled vs plain text completions. 3) Reproduce at scale by sending 1000 requests/min with a similar request shape. Observed behavior: median latency for tool-enabled completions is ~180ms higher than baseline; P95 increased from ~420ms to ~1.1s and P99 spikes up to 2.4s. Traces show multiple 50-250ms synchronous gaps attributed to function-proxy handshake and repeated "schema.compile" calls. Expected behavior: handshake should be <50ms and schema validation should be cached/reused to avoid per-call compilation. Logs/Traces: Attached (file references in ticket) - trace ids: trace-us-east-20260312-abc123, trace-us-east-20260313-def456. Validator logs contain repeated: "schema.compile: cache_miss=true, compile_time_ms=82" on every invocation. Function-proxy logs show handshake RTTs of 40-220ms during spikes. Additional notes: issue concentrated on requests with multiple short tool calls; single tool-call flows less impacted. Occurs during customer peak traffic and correlates with recent proxy validator deployment (2026-03-11).
investigation_notes: Initial findings: 1) Histogram and flame graphs point to two dominant contributors: synchronous proxy handshake (blocking wait for tool adapter readiness) and per-invocation JSON schema compile inside the schema-validator process. 2) Schema validator recently changed from 'compile-on-first-use' with LRU cache to 'compile-every-request' due to a bugfix intended to enforce strict validation isolation for enterprise tenants. 3) The function-proxy handshake includes a synchronous SSL/TLS handshake and a metadata exchange; in our code path this is done inline on the request critical path. Data points: p95 latency delta = +680ms for affected requests; during one spike we saw 12% of requests with 2+ handshake events >150ms. Hypotheses: A) schema.compile is CPU-bound and when cache_miss=True it costs ~80-120ms and spikes under CPU contention; B) synchronous proxy handshake amplifies tail when combined with multiple sequential tool calls; C) lack of schema caching and blocking sync calls produce multiplicative effect for sequences of short tools. Temporary mitigations attempted: turned on schema_validator debug logs (no change), increased validator worker pool from 8->12 (reduced median slightly), enabled per-tenant adapter warm-up for a subset of routes (reduced handshake occurrences but not eliminated). Correlation with PR: serving-runtime PR #1843 touched proxy handshake retry logic and may have affected connection reuse behavior. Traces and flame graphs shared in ticket attachments.

2026-03-13 14:41 - Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Confirmed regression introduced by change to validator cache policy in enterprise path. Drafting hotfix to re-enable per-tenant schema cache with isolation guard.
2026-03-14 08:30 - AcmePayments (Customer): Customer notes that timeouts up to 3s caused a small % of transactions to be retried client-side; asking for ETA on fix and temporary workaround.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-14 09:10 UTC): rolled out a targeted hotfix to function-proxy in us-east-1 for AcmePayments tenant that introduces an in-memory schema cache keyed by tool signature and an async handshake fast-path. Behavior: per-invocation compile cache hits eliminated for common tool signatures, and handshake now uses connection warm-pool to avoid blocking on first-request TLS handshake. Immediate effect: P95 for affected routes dropped from ~1.1s to ~520ms in canary. Planned next steps: 1) publish patch to all enterprise tenants in us-east (canary -> gradual rollout), 2) add metrics (schema.compile.cache_hit, proxy.handshake_time_ms) to monitoring and dashboards, 3) backport safe cache behavior to older runtime branches, 4) add automated perf regression test in CI that exercises multi-tool sequences. Timeline: canary applied 2026-03-14 09:10 UTC, global rollout planned for 2026-03-16 pending telemetry. If rollback needed we have rollback plan to disable cache and revert handshake changes via runtime feature flag.
